div.div: كِسَآءٌ مَنْبَجَانِىٌّ , (S, K,) the latter word being formed after the manner of مَخْبَرَانِىٌّ and مَنْظَرَانِىٌّ, (S,) and ↓ أَنْبَجَانِىٌّ , rel. ns. of مَنْبِجٌ, each with fet-hah to the ب, contr. to analogy, (K,) the latter disallowed by IKt, but occurring in a trad. and in poetry, and not to be disallowed because contr. to analogy, since there are many such rel. ns., as مَرْوَزِىٌّ and رَازِىٌّ &c., (TA,) A certain kind of كساء, so called in relation to a place named مَنْبِجٌ: (S, K, &c.:) or كساء أَنْبَجَانِىٌّ, and أَنْبِجَانِىٌّ, which latter form is related by IAth as the one retained in the memory, a certain kind of كساء, so called in relation to a place named انبجان; of wool, having a nap, or pile, without a border; one of the meanest kinds of coarse garments: its ا, accord. to some, is an augmentative letter. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
